title: Nonce-Based Adaptive-Compromise Security
summary: Known analysis extensions cover standard randomized symmetric encryption with idealized components; their applicability to nonce-based schemes remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Analysis-extension techniques are known for showing that most standard randomized symmetric encryption schemes satisfy adaptive-compromise security definitions when their underlying components are appropriately idealized. Determine whether these techniques extend to nonce-based encryption schemes and yield security under the corresponding nonce-based adaptive-compromise definitions under the same idealization condition.

scope.domain: Adaptive-compromise security of randomized and nonce-based symmetric encryption schemes.
parameters: nonce-based encryption schemes as the target construction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the analysis-extension techniques extend to nonce-based encryption schemes and yield security under the corresponding nonce-based adaptive-compromise definitions under the same idealization condition.

citations.label: Handling Adaptive Compromise for Practical Encryption Schemes

progress.summary: The source presents this as a security conjecture, noting that techniques from Sections 5 and 6 establish the relevant analysis extensions for standard randomized schemes and conjecturing that the same ideas apply to nonce-based schemes.
citation_labels: Joseph Jaeger et al., Handling Adaptive Compromise for Practical Encryption Schemes
